## Load required libraries

```{r cars}

library(dplyr)
library(visdat)
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)

```



## Load the shipment dataset into R
```{r echo=FALSE}

shipment  <- readr::read_csv("shipment_Dataset.csv")

head(shipment, 10)
tail(shipment, 10)
colnames(shipment)

shipment <- clean_names(shipment)

View(shipment)
```
The shipment data set has `dim(shipment)` rows, columns


##Descriptive Analysis
```{r}
#Showing the statistics of the shipment dataset
summary(shipment)


#Showing the structure of the shipment dataset
str(shipment)

#visual display of datatype
visdat::vis_dat(shipment)

```

Rows: 2508 Columns: 17 
The column names and types: `spec(shipment)`



## Clean dataset
```{r echo=FALSE}

visdat::vis_miss(shipment)

sum(is.na(shipment$City))

sum(is.na(shipment$customer_name))

```
Most of the dataset has values. Only less than 1% is not available. These are in the customer name and city columns
1. There are `sum(is.na(shipment$City))` null values in the City column
2. There are `sum(is.na(shipment$customer_name))` null values in the Customer name column


## Analysis
Access Performance: 
Understand monthly sales, profit and profitability trends.
```{r echo=FALSE}
names(shipment) 

#monthly sales
  shipment %>% select(order_date,sales) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(order_date),
    month = month(order_date),
    month_name = month(order_date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)
  ) %>% 
  order_by(desc(year))


```
